source: Code titles follow the generic SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6 definitions (paraphrased). Explanations, possible causes and tests are general guidance written for OpenDiag, not manufacturer data; always check the vehicle's own documentation.

codes.title: "A" Camshaft position actuator circuit (bank 1)
codes.plain: The engine computer sees an electrical problem in the circuit that controls the intake camshaft timing.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the actuator connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance against specification

codes.title: "A" Camshaft position: timing over-advanced or system performance (bank 1)
codes.plain: The intake camshaft timing is not where the engine computer expects it.
possible_causes: Stretched timing chain or worn tensioner
suggested_tests: Check oil level and condition
Check service history for the oil change interval
Inspect the timing solenoid and its oil screen
codes.driving_advice: Check the oil level before driving further.

codes.title: Crankshaft / camshaft position correlation (bank 1 sensor A)
codes.plain: The crankshaft and camshaft signals are out of step with each other.
possible_causes: Stretched timing chain/belt or jumped tooth
suggested_tests: Check for related camshaft codes
Verify mechanical timing marks (consult documentation)
Check sensor signals with an oscilloscope
codes.driving_advice: Timing problems can cause serious engine damage. Avoid driving until checked.

codes.title: MAP / MAF to throttle position correlation
codes.plain: The air flow readings do not match what the throttle position suggests.
possible_causes: Faulty air flow or manifold pressure sensor
suggested_tests: Inspect for intake leaks
Compare MAP, MAF and throttle readings at idle

codes.title: Fuel rail / system pressure too low
codes.plain: The fuel pressure in the rail is below what the engine computer commanded.
possible_causes: Weak fuel pump or high-pressure pump
suggested_tests: Read fuel rail pressure in live data
Check the fuel filter service history
Inspect for leaks
codes.driving_advice: Low fuel pressure can cause power loss or stalling.

codes.title: Fuel rail / system pressure too high
codes.plain: The fuel pressure in the rail is above the commanded value.
possible_causes: Faulty pressure regulator or control valve
Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Read fuel rail pressure in live data
Inspect the regulator wiring

codes.title: Mass or volume air flow sensor circuit
codes.plain: The engine computer sees a problem in the air flow sensor circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
Air leak between the sensor and the engine
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor connector
Check the air flow reading at idle

codes.title: Mass or volume air flow sensor range/performance
codes.plain: The air flow sensor reading is not plausible for the engine's operating conditions.
possible_causes: Dirty or contaminated air flow sensor
suggested_tests: Inspect the air filter and intake ducting
Compare the air flow reading with load and engine speed

codes.title: Mass or volume air flow sensor circuit low
codes.plain: The air flow sensor signal is lower than possible.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector (open or short to ground)
Large air leak after the sensor
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's supply and signal wiring

codes.title: Mass or volume air flow sensor circuit high
codes.plain: The air flow sensor signal is higher than possible.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector (short to voltage)
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's signal wiring

codes.title: Manifold absolute pressure / barometric pressure range/performance
codes.plain: The manifold pressure reading is not plausible.
possible_causes: Vacuum leak or blocked sensor hose
suggested_tests: Compare MAP with barometric pressure with the engine off (they should be similar)

codes.title: Manifold absolute pressure circuit low
codes.plain: The manifold pressure sensor signal is too low.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's 5 V reference and signal

codes.title: Manifold absolute pressure circuit high
codes.plain: The manifold pressure sensor signal is too high.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's signal wiring

codes.title: Intake air temperature sensor circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the intake air temperature sensor circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Compare the reading with ambient temperature on a cold engine

codes.title: Intake air temperature sensor circuit low
codes.plain: The intake air temperature signal is too low (reads very hot).
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector (short to ground)
suggested_tests: Check the reading on a cold engine

codes.title: Intake air temperature sensor circuit high
codes.plain: The intake air temperature signal is too high (reads very cold, often -40 °C).
suggested_tests: Check the sensor connector
Check the reading on a cold engine

codes.title: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the coolant temperature sensor circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Compare the reading with actual engine temperature

codes.title: Engine coolant temperature sensor range/performance
codes.plain: The coolant temperature reading is not plausible.
suggested_tests: Watch coolant temperature in live data while the engine warms up

codes.title: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit low
codes.plain: The coolant temperature signal is too low (reads very hot).
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector (short to ground)
suggested_tests: Check the reading on a cold engine

codes.title: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit high
codes.plain: The coolant temperature signal is too high (reads very cold).
suggested_tests: Check the sensor connector

codes.title: Throttle/pedal position sensor A circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the throttle or pedal position sensor A circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Watch throttle position while slowly pressing the pedal (engine off, ignition on): it should change smoothly
codes.driving_advice: The engine may go into a reduced-power mode.

codes.title: Throttle/pedal position sensor A range/performance
codes.plain: The throttle position reading is not plausible.
suggested_tests: Watch throttle position for jumps while slowly moving the pedal

codes.title: Throttle/pedal position sensor A circuit low
codes.plain: The throttle position signal is too low.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's reference voltage and signal

codes.title: Throttle/pedal position sensor A circuit high
codes.plain: The throttle position signal is too high.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the sensor's signal wiring

codes.title: Insufficient coolant temperature for closed loop fuel control
codes.plain: The engine takes too long to warm up enough for normal fuel control.
suggested_tests: Watch coolant temperature: a healthy engine usually reaches operating temperature within 10–20 minutes of driving

codes.title: Coolant thermostat (coolant temperature below thermostat regulating temperature)
codes.plain: The engine does not reach its normal temperature in the expected time.
possible_causes: Cooling fan running all the time
suggested_tests: Watch coolant temperature while driving
Check whether the cooling fan runs on a cold engine

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: There is a problem in the circuit of the front oxygen sensor on bank 1.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Watch the sensor voltage: a narrow-band sensor normally switches between about 0.1 V and 0.9 V when warm

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit low voltage (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: The front oxygen sensor voltage stays too low.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check fuel trims and the sensor voltage

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit high voltage (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: The front oxygen sensor voltage stays too high.
suggested_tests: Check fuel trims and the sensor voltage

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit slow response (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: The front oxygen sensor reacts too slowly.
suggested_tests: Watch how quickly the sensor voltage switches

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit no activity detected (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: The front oxygen sensor signal does not change.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the sensor voltage with a warm engine

codes.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
codes.plain: The heater inside the front oxygen sensor has an electrical fault.
possible_causes: Blown fuse for the heater circuit
Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the heater fuse
Measure heater resistance against specification

codes.title: O2 sensor circuit (bank 1 sensor 2)
codes.plain: There is a problem in the circuit of the rear oxygen sensor on bank 1.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Watch the rear sensor voltage: after a working catalyst it is usually fairly steady

codes.title: O2 sensor heater circuit (bank 1 sensor 2)
codes.plain: The heater inside the rear oxygen sensor has an electrical fault.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the heater fuse
Measure heater resistance against specification

codes.title: System too lean (bank 1)
codes.plain: The engine computer is adding a lot of extra fuel on bank 1 to keep the mixture right, which means too much air or too little fuel is getting in.
possible_causes: Air leak after the air flow sensor (vacuum hose, intake gasket, crankcase breather)
Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Low fuel pressure (weak pump, clogged filter, faulty regulator)
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor
suggested_tests: Compare short and long term fuel trims at idle and at 2500 rpm: trims that improve with engine speed point to a vacuum leak, trims that worsen point to fuel delivery
Listen and check for vacuum leaks
Check the air flow reading against the engine size and speed (consult documentation)
Measure fuel pressure against the vehicle's specification
codes.driving_advice: Usually safe to drive short distances, but long-term lean running can damage the engine or catalyst.

codes.title: System too rich (bank 1)
codes.plain: The engine computer is taking away a lot of fuel on bank 1, which means too much fuel or too little air is getting in.
possible_causes: Faulty coolant temperature sensor reading too cold
Faulty or contaminated air flow sensor
suggested_tests: Check fuel trims and oxygen sensor readings
Compare coolant temperature reading with actual engine temperature
Inspect air filter
Measure fuel pressure against specification

codes.title: System too lean (bank 2)
codes.plain: Like P0171, but on bank 2 (the side of a V engine without cylinder 1).
possible_causes: Air leak after the air flow sensor (vacuum hose, intake gasket, crankcase breather)
Dirty or faulty mass air flow sensor
Low fuel pressure (weak pump, clogged filter, faulty regulator)
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor
suggested_tests: Compare short and long term fuel trims at idle and at 2500 rpm: trims that improve with engine speed point to a vacuum leak, trims that worsen point to fuel delivery
Listen and check for vacuum leaks
Check the air flow reading against the engine size and speed (consult documentation)
Measure fuel pressure against the vehicle's specification

codes.title: System too rich (bank 2)
codes.plain: Like P0172, but on bank 2.
possible_causes: Faulty coolant temperature sensor reading too cold
Faulty or contaminated air flow sensor
suggested_tests: Check fuel trims and oxygen sensor readings
Compare coolant temperature reading with actual engine temperature
Inspect air filter
Measure fuel pressure against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in an injector circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
Injector driver fault in the engine control module
suggested_tests: Check for cylinder-specific injector or misfire codes

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 1
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 1.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 2
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 2.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 3
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 3.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 4
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 4.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 5
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 5.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Injector circuit, cylinder 6
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the injector circuit of cylinder 6.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the injector connector
Measure injector resistance against specification

codes.title: Engine coolant over temperature condition
codes.plain: The engine has been too hot.
suggested_tests: Check coolant level only when the engine is cold
Watch coolant temperature and fan operation
codes.driving_advice: Stop the engine as soon as it is safe. Overheating can destroy an engine.

codes.title: Fuel pump primary circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the fuel pump control circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check the fuel pump fuse and relay
codes.driving_advice: The engine may not start or may stall.

codes.title: Turbocharger/supercharger "A" overboost condition
codes.plain: Boost pressure has gone above the allowed limit.
possible_causes: Sticking wastegate or variable vane mechanism
suggested_tests: Watch manifold pressure under load
Inspect the boost control hoses
codes.driving_advice: Avoid hard acceleration until checked.

codes.title: Turbocharger/supercharger "A" underboost condition
codes.plain: The turbocharger is not producing the boost the engine computer asked for.
possible_causes: Boost leak (split hose, loose clamp, intercooler leak)
suggested_tests: Listen for hissing under load
Inspect intercooler hoses and clamps
Watch manifold pressure under load

codes.title: Random/multiple cylinder misfire detected
codes.plain: The engine computer detects misfires that are not limited to one cylinder.
suggested_tests: Read cylinder-specific misfire codes
Check fuel trims
Inspect spark plugs
codes.driving_advice: A flashing check-engine light means severe misfire that can damage the catalyst: reduce load and have it checked.

codes.title: Cylinder 1 misfire detected
codes.plain: Cylinder 1 is not burning its fuel properly.
possible_causes: Faulty ignition coil or plug lead
suggested_tests: Inspect the spark plug for that cylinder
Swap the ignition coil with another cylinder and see if the misfire moves
Check injector wiring and resistance against specification
Perform a compression test
codes.driving_advice: A flashing check-engine light means severe misfire that can damage the catalyst: reduce load and have it checked.

codes.title: Ignition / distributor engine speed input circuit
codes.plain: The engine computer sees a problem with the engine speed signal (on most modern engines it comes from the crankshaft position sensor).
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Inspect the crankshaft sensor connector and wiring
Check the sensor's signal with an oscilloscope or meter against specification
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Ignition / distributor engine speed input circuit range/performance
codes.plain: The engine speed signal is present but does not make sense, for example it drops out or jumps.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor, its air gap and the trigger wheel
Check the wiring for chafing near hot or moving parts
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Ignition / distributor engine speed input circuit no signal
codes.plain: The engine computer received no engine speed signal at a moment it expected one. On most modern engines this signal comes from the crankshaft position sensor.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Inspect the crankshaft sensor connector and wiring for damage, corrosion and loose pins
Measure the sensor (resistance or signal) against specification
Check the battery and charging voltage
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Knock sensor 1 circuit (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the knock sensor circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring

codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor "A" circuit
codes.plain: The engine computer has a problem with the crankshaft position signal.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Check whether engine speed shows while cranking
codes.driving_advice: The engine may stall or not start.

codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor "A" circuit range/performance
codes.plain: The crankshaft sensor signal is present but irregular or implausible.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor, its mounting and the trigger wheel
Check the wiring and connector
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor "A" circuit low
codes.plain: The crankshaft sensor signal stays too low, usually an electrical fault.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Check the wiring for a short to ground
Inspect the connector
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor "A" circuit high
codes.plain: The crankshaft sensor signal stays too high, usually an electrical fault.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Check the wiring for an open circuit or a short to voltage
Inspect the connector
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Crankshaft position sensor "A" circuit intermittent
codes.plain: The crankshaft sensor signal comes and goes.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector at the sensor
Dirt or metal debris on the sensor tip, or a damaged reluctor (trigger) wheel
suggested_tests: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector while watching engine speed
Inspect for chafed wiring
codes.driving_advice: The engine may cut out or not start. Avoid driving in traffic until it is checked.

codes.title: Camshaft position sensor "A" circuit (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: The engine computer has a problem with the camshaft position signal.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor connector
Check for crank/cam correlation codes

codes.title: Camshaft position sensor "A" circuit range/performance (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: The camshaft sensor signal is present but does not match the crankshaft signal as expected.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring, a loose/corroded connector, or a supply/ground fault shared with other sensors
Camshaft timing out of position (worn or jumped timing belt/chain) for range/performance faults
suggested_tests: Inspect the camshaft sensor and wiring
If the code returns, have the camshaft timing (belt/chain) checked

codes.title: Camshaft position sensor "A" circuit low (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: The camshaft sensor signal stays too low, usually an electrical fault.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring, a loose/corroded connector, or a supply/ground fault shared with other sensors
Camshaft timing out of position (worn or jumped timing belt/chain) for range/performance faults
suggested_tests: Check the wiring for a short to ground
Check the sensor's supply voltage

codes.title: Camshaft position sensor "A" circuit high (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: The camshaft sensor signal stays too high, usually an open circuit, a bad connection or a sensor fault.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring, a loose/corroded connector, or a supply/ground fault shared with other sensors
Camshaft timing out of position (worn or jumped timing belt/chain) for range/performance faults
suggested_tests: Inspect the camshaft sensor connector and wiring for an open circuit
Check the sensor's supply and ground
Replace the sensor only after the wiring checks out

codes.title: Camshaft position sensor "A" circuit intermittent (bank 1 or single sensor)
codes.plain: The camshaft sensor signal comes and goes.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring, a loose/corroded connector, or a supply/ground fault shared with other sensors
Camshaft timing out of position (worn or jumped timing belt/chain) for range/performance faults
suggested_tests: Wiggle-test the wiring and connector
Inspect for chafed wiring near the timing cover

codes.title: Glow plug/heater circuit "A"
codes.plain: There is a problem in the glow plug circuit (diesel).
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Measure each glow plug's resistance against specification
codes.driving_advice: Starting may be hard in cold weather.

codes.title: Exhaust gas recirculation flow
codes.plain: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) flow is not as expected.
suggested_tests: Inspect the EGR valve for carbon build-up

codes.title: Exhaust gas recirculation flow insufficient detected
codes.plain: Less exhaust gas is being recirculated than expected.
possible_causes: Faulty EGR valve or position sensor
suggested_tests: Inspect the EGR valve and passages
Check the EGR valve operates when commanded (consult documentation)

codes.title: Exhaust gas recirculation flow excessive detected
codes.plain: More exhaust gas is being recirculated than expected.
suggested_tests: Check for rough idle
Inspect the EGR valve

codes.title: Exhaust gas recirculation control circuit
codes.plain: There is an electrical problem in the EGR control circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the EGR connector
Measure the solenoid resistance against specification

codes.title: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold (bank 1)
codes.plain: The catalytic converter on bank 1 is not cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
possible_causes: Engine misfire or rich running that damaged the catalyst
suggested_tests: Fix any misfire or fuel trim codes first
Compare front and rear oxygen sensor signals: the rear should be much steadier
Check for exhaust leaks

codes.title: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold (bank 2)
codes.plain: Like P0420, but on bank 2.
suggested_tests: Compare front and rear oxygen sensor signals on bank 2

codes.title: Evaporative emission system
codes.plain: There is a problem in the system that captures fuel vapour from the tank.
possible_causes: Loose or faulty fuel filler cap
suggested_tests: Check the fuel cap seal
Inspect evaporative hoses

codes.title: Evaporative emission system incorrect purge flow
codes.plain: The purge flow of the fuel vapour system is not as expected.
suggested_tests: Inspect the purge valve and hoses

codes.title: Evaporative emission system leak detected (small leak)
codes.plain: A small leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
suggested_tests: Check the fuel cap seal
A smoke test finds small leaks

codes.title: Evaporative emission system vent control circuit
codes.plain: There is a problem in the vent valve circuit of the fuel vapour system.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the vent valve and its filter

codes.title: Evaporative emission system leak detected (large leak)
codes.plain: A large leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
suggested_tests: Check the fuel cap first
Inspect evaporative hoses

codes.title: Evaporative emission system leak detected (very small leak)
codes.plain: A very small leak was found in the fuel vapour system.
possible_causes: Tiny crack in a hose or seal
suggested_tests: A smoke test finds very small leaks

codes.title: Vehicle speed sensor "A"
codes.plain: The engine computer does not get a valid vehicle speed signal.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
Missing signal from the ABS module (on many vehicles)
suggested_tests: Check whether vehicle speed shows in live data while driving
Check the ABS module for codes
codes.driving_advice: Speedometer, cruise control and gear shifting may be affected.

codes.title: Idle air control system
codes.plain: The engine cannot control the idle speed properly.
possible_causes: Dirty throttle body or idle valve
suggested_tests: Watch idle speed in live data
Inspect for vacuum leaks

codes.title: Idle air control system RPM lower than expected
codes.plain: The idle speed is lower than the target.
suggested_tests: Inspect and clean the throttle body following the manufacturer's procedure

codes.title: Idle air control system RPM higher than expected
codes.plain: The idle speed is higher than the target.
suggested_tests: Inspect for vacuum leaks

codes.title: System voltage
codes.plain: The supply voltage seen by the engine computer is not plausible.
suggested_tests: Measure battery voltage with the engine off and running

codes.title: System voltage low
codes.plain: The supply voltage seen by the control module is too low.
possible_causes: Corroded battery terminals or poor ground
High electrical load (e.g. accessories) at low engine speed
suggested_tests: Measure battery voltage with the engine off (a charged lead-acid battery is usually about 12.4–12.7 V; general guidance)
Measure voltage with the engine running (charging systems usually give about 13.5–14.7 V; general guidance, check the vehicle's specification)
Inspect battery terminals and ground straps
codes.driving_advice: Low voltage can cause starting problems and other electrical faults.

codes.title: System voltage high
codes.plain: The supply voltage seen by the control module is too high.
suggested_tests: Measure voltage with the engine running
codes.driving_advice: Overvoltage can damage electronics. Have the charging system checked soon.

codes.title: Serial communication link
codes.plain: The engine computer has a problem communicating with another module.
suggested_tests: Check other modules for communication codes

codes.title: Internal control module memory checksum error
codes.plain: The engine computer found an error in its own memory.
suggested_tests: Have the module checked by a qualified professional
codes.driving_advice: This is a module fault; do not attempt reprogramming without the manufacturer's tools.

codes.title: Control module processor
codes.plain: The engine computer detected an internal processor fault.
possible_causes: Supply or ground problem to the module
suggested_tests: Check the module's power and ground circuits
Have the module checked by a qualified professional

codes.title: Transmission control system (MIL request)
codes.plain: The transmission computer has stored a fault and asked for the warning light.
suggested_tests: Read the transmission module's own codes

codes.title: Input/turbine speed sensor "A" circuit
codes.plain: The transmission computer has a problem with the input shaft speed signal.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor connector
Check transmission fluid level following the manufacturer's procedure
codes.driving_advice: Gear shifting may be harsh or the transmission may go into a limp mode.

codes.title: Output speed sensor circuit
codes.plain: The transmission computer has a problem with the output shaft speed signal.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Inspect the sensor connector

codes.title: Incorrect gear ratio
codes.plain: The transmission's input and output speeds do not match any expected gear.
suggested_tests: Check transmission fluid level and condition following the manufacturer's procedure
Check for speed sensor codes
codes.driving_advice: Driving with a slipping transmission can cause more damage.

codes.title: Torque converter clutch circuit
codes.plain: There is a problem in the torque converter lock-up clutch circuit.
possible_causes: Damaged wiring or a loose/corroded connector
suggested_tests: Read the transmission module's codes

codes.title: Replace hybrid battery pack
codes.plain: The hybrid system computer reports that the high-voltage battery pack is degraded.
possible_causes: Weak cells or modules in the hybrid battery
suggested_tests: Have the high-voltage system checked by a qualified professional
codes.driving_advice: High-voltage systems can be lethal. Do not open the battery or orange cables without training.

codes.title: Diesel particulate filter efficiency below threshold (bank 1)
codes.plain: The diesel particulate filter does not seem to be trapping soot properly.
possible_causes: Faulty differential pressure sensor or its hoses
suggested_tests: Inspect the pressure sensor hoses
Check for other particulate filter codes

codes.title: Post catalyst fuel trim system too lean (bank 1)
codes.plain: The rear oxygen sensor shows the mixture is lean after the catalyst.
possible_causes: Exhaust leak near the rear sensor
suggested_tests: Check for exhaust leaks
Check fuel trims

codes.title: Post catalyst fuel trim system too rich (bank 1)
codes.plain: The rear oxygen sensor shows the mixture is rich after the catalyst.
suggested_tests: Check fuel trims and oxygen sensors

codes.title: Diesel particulate filter restriction: ash accumulation
codes.plain: The particulate filter is filling up with ash, which regeneration cannot burn off.
suggested_tests: Check the service history for the filter
Consult a qualified professional about cleaning or replacement

codes.title: Lost communication with ECM/PCM "A"
codes.plain: Another module stopped hearing the engine computer on the vehicle network.
possible_causes: Engine computer without power or ground
suggested_tests: Check whether the engine computer answers this scan
Check battery voltage
Inspect network wiring and connectors

codes.title: Lost communication with TCM
codes.plain: A module stopped hearing the transmission computer.
suggested_tests: Check the transmission module's fuses and connectors

codes.title: Lost communication with anti-lock brake system (ABS) control module
codes.plain: A module stopped hearing the ABS computer.
suggested_tests: Check ABS fuses
Check whether the ABS warning light is on
codes.driving_advice: ABS and stability control may not work. Drive carefully and have it checked.

codes.title: Lost communication with body control module
codes.plain: A module stopped hearing the body control module.
suggested_tests: Check the body control module's fuses

codes.title: Lost communication with instrument panel cluster (IPC) control module
codes.plain: A module stopped hearing the instrument cluster.
suggested_tests: Check the cluster's fuses and connector
